evidence.note: This contemporaneous company disclosure supports the firm component concerning OpenAI's public training policy. It establishes neither payment arrangements nor the legal validity of the fair-use position.
The reported AP licensing payment qualifies the payment inference and counters a blanket nonpayment interpretation. Selective licensing does not contradict rejection of universal licensing.

reviews.rationale: The payment allegation is explicitly tentative and has no definite scope, so the compound claim cannot receive a scored verdict under the policy. OpenAI's disclosure supports the firm policy component; the AP payment limits any broad nonpayment inference without establishing comprehensive licensing.
